boards.school_name: SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry
boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named SUNY ESF campus spaces with documented ways students can study, connect, get support, or encounter the College’s work.

cards.title: Moon Library
cards.subtitle: 1 Forestry Drive, SUNY ESF
cards.notes: Set up at the movable tables or living-space seating between classes, then use the service desk for circulation, reserves, or research help.
cards.short_summary: A flexible academic hub with workstations, rearrangeable tables, and lounge-style seating.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF describes Moon Library as the campus’s academic living room, with computer workstations, movable tables and chairs, and living spaces with reclining chairs and couches.
cards.access_notes: Library access and services follow Moon Library’s current policies and hours.

cards.title: Academic Success Center
cards.subtitle: Room 009, Moon Library
cards.notes: Bring a draft, a course question, or a study plan; the center offers peer tutoring, drop-in writing support, computers, and graduate-school resources.
cards.short_summary: A Moon Library support space for tutoring, writing help, study resources, and computers.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF states that the Academic Success Center in 009 Moon Library provides peer tutoring, drop-in writing support, success resources, a computer lab, and graduate-school preparation resources.
cards.source_title: Academic Success and Integrity Information | SUNY ESF
cards.access_notes: Services are for ESF students; check the Academic Success Center for current appointment and drop-in availability.

cards.title: MOSAIC Lounge
cards.subtitle: Lower level, Moon Library
cards.notes: Use this designated lower-level lounge when you need a student-centered place to pause, meet briefly, or work near other campus services.
cards.short_summary: A named student lounge in Moon Library’s designated after-hours area.
cards.evidence_claim: Moon Library’s 24/7 access policy lists the MOSAIC Lounge among the lower-level spaces available after hours.
cards.access_notes: After-hours access requires an active ESF affiliation, valid ESF ID, and activated access; remain in designated areas.

cards.title: ESF Interfaith Space
cards.subtitle: First floor, Moon Library
cards.notes: Use the room for prayer, meditation, or quiet reflection; leave lounge, meeting, and general study activities for other campus spaces.
cards.short_summary: A private, religiously neutral room for prayer, meditation, and reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF identifies the Interfaith Space as a religiously neutral prayer and meditation room on Moon Library’s first floor, open during regular library hours.
cards.source_title: Interfaith Space | SUNY ESF Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Open and unlocked during regular library business hours; intended only for prayer, meditation, and reflection.

cards.title: Moon Library Lobby
cards.subtitle: Moon Library, SUNY ESF
cards.notes: For a late assignment session, activate your ESF ID first and use the lobby only within the library’s designated after-hours access rules.
cards.short_summary: A designated Moon Library area available to authorized ESF community members after regular hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Beginning February 15, 2026, ESF’s 24/7 program extends access to the Moon Lobby as a study space when the library is otherwise closed.
cards.access_notes: Available after hours only to active ESF students, faculty, and staff with valid, activated ESF ID; follow the 24/7 community guidelines.

cards.title: Gateway Center
cards.subtitle: SUNY ESF main campus
cards.notes: Meet classmates at a concourse table, browse the specimen display, or use the building as a central starting point before a campus event.
cards.short_summary: A campus hub with a large open concourse, seating, exhibits, events, and food service.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF says Gateway Center provides students space to gather and socialize, with tables and chairs in its open concourse, exhibition space, and event facilities.
cards.access_notes: Public-facing building amenities and event access can vary; follow posted building and event guidance.

cards.title: Gateway Center Green Roof
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Gateway Center
cards.notes: Take a study break at the seating areas and notice how the roof is part of the building’s sustainability features before returning to the concourse.
cards.short_summary: A planted Gateway Center roof with seating areas for food, studying, and socializing.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF states that food, study, and socializing can be enjoyed on Gateway Center’s green roof, which has seating areas.
cards.access_notes: Use only when the roof is open and follow any posted access rules.

cards.title: Trailhead Café
cards.subtitle: First floor, Gateway Center
cards.notes: Use the Gateway café as a planned food stop, then carry your work or conversation to the adjacent concourse or green-roof seating.
cards.short_summary: The Gateway Center café, located beside spaces for gathering, studying, and socializing.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF’s campus tour identifies Trailhead Café in Gateway Center and says the surrounding green roof and concourse support food, study, and socializing.
cards.access_notes: Food and beverages are sold; verify current service availability before visiting.

cards.title: Roosevelt Wildlife Collection Display
cards.subtitle: Gateway Center main concourse
cards.notes: Pause at the concourse display to look closely at ESF’s wildlife specimens, then connect what you see with the College’s field-study and collection work.
cards.short_summary: A Gateway Center specimen display drawn from ESF’s Roosevelt Wildlife Collection.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF’s campus tour lists exhibition space for specimens from the College’s Roosevelt Wildlife Collection in Gateway Center, and ESF documented a collection display in its main concourse.
cards.access_notes: View the display during building access hours; exhibits may change.

cards.title: Digital Storytelling Studio
cards.subtitle: First floor, Marshall Hall
cards.notes: Bring a class project needing audio, visuals, editing, or a story map; the studio provides equipment loans and computers for digital work.
cards.short_summary: A Marshall Hall workspace for composing, editing, and developing digital science and environmental stories.
cards.evidence_claim: ESF says the Digital Storytelling Studio in Marshall Hall offers free storytelling services, equipment loans, four computers with editing software, and space for student digital projects.
cards.source_title: ESF Celebrates Debut of Digital Storytelling Studio
cards.access_notes: Confirm current studio staffing, equipment-loan procedures, and access before planning a project session.
